questions.text: Emperor Menilek II unified the northern and central parts of Ethiopia while also expanding territorially into the south.
questions.explanation: The making of modern Ethiopia involved unification of northern/north-central regions and territorial expansion into the south, continued under Menilek.

questions.text: The two major 19th century long-distance trade routes in Ethiopia both started from which market centre?
questions.explanation: Both major trade routes started from Bonga, the capital of the Kafa Kingdom.

questions.text: Which coin, introduced from Austria via Arab traders, served as a medium of exchange alongside salt bars?
questions.explanation: The Maria Theresa Thaler (MTT) was introduced from Austria to the Horn of Africa and served as a medium of exchange.

questions.text: Which group of merchants were described as northern Muslim merchants dominant in the long-distance trade?
questions.explanation: The northern Muslim merchants were known as Jabarti.

questions.text: Which item was NOT among the principal commodities of 19th century long-distance trade, according to the unit?
questions.explanation: The principal commodities were ivory, civet musk, salt bars (amole), and slaves — coffee is not listed.

questions.text: Who was the first modern emperor to attempt the unification of Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: Tewodros II (1855-1868), formerly Kassa Hailu of Quara, was the first emperor to attempt to unify the country.

questions.text: At which battle was the last ruler of the Yejju dynasty defeated, symbolizing the end of the Zemene Mesafint?
questions.explanation: The battle of Ayshal, where the last ruler of the Yejju dynasty was defeated, symbolized the end of Zemene Mesafint.

questions.text: Where did Tewodros II establish his arms manufacturing centre with European missionaries and artisans?
questions.explanation: Tewodros established an arms manufacture at Gafat, near Debre Tabor.

questions.text: What was the name of Tewodros II's famous mortar produced at Gafat?
questions.explanation: His famous mortar produced at Gafat was known as 'Sebastopol'.

questions.text: How did Emperor Tewodros II's reign come to an end in 1868?

options.text: He committed suicide after the British stormed Maqdala
He was assassinated by Yohannes IV

questions.explanation: The storming of Meqdela by the British and the subsequent suicide of Tewodros brought an end to his reign.

questions.text: Through which agreement did Yohannes IV recognize Menilek as Nigus of Shewa in 1878?
questions.explanation: Yohannes IV recognized Menilek as Nigus of Shewa in 1878 by the Liche agreement.

questions.text: At the Council of Boru Meda (1878), what did Emperor Yohannes IV declare regarding the Ethiopian Orthodox Church?

options.text: That Islam would be the state religion
That Tewahdo was the only doctrine of the EOTC
That the church would be abolished

questions.explanation: Yohannes IV presided over the Council of Boru Meda, where Tewahdo was declared the only doctrine of the EOTC.

questions.text: How did Emperor Yohannes IV die in 1889?
questions.explanation: On 9 March 1889, Yohannes marched to Metemma where he died fighting the Mahdists.

questions.text: Which Shewan Oromo notable played a pivotal role in Menilek's territorial expansion?
questions.explanation: The Shewan Oromo notable Ras Gobana Dache played a pivotal role in territorial expansion and creation of the modern empire.

questions.text: Who led the resistance of the western Gurage against Menilek's forces until their defeat in 1888?
questions.explanation: The western Gurage, led by Hassan Enjamo of Qabena, strongly resisted Menilek's forces until defeated in 1888.

questions.text: At which battle was Ras Adal (Nigus Tekle-Haymanot) defeated by Ras Gobana, opening the way to western Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: Ras Adal was defeated at Embabo by Menilek's commander Ras Gobana.

questions.text: It took six campaigns from 1882 to 1886 and the battle of Azule to pacify which people?
questions.explanation: It took six campaigns from 1882 to 1886 to pacify the Arsi Oromo, ending at the battle of Azule in 1886.

questions.text: At the battle of Chalanqo (1887), the combined forces of which two groups resisted Menilek's expansion into Hararghe?
questions.explanation: In Hararghe, the combined forces of the Harari and the Oromo attempted to resist Menilek's expansion, defeated at Chalanqo.

questions.text: Who was appointed governor of Hararghe by Menilek II after the battle of Chalanqo?
questions.explanation: Dejjach (later Ras) Mekonnen Welde-Mikael was appointed governor of Hararghe after the battle of Chalanqo.

questions.text: What was the immediate cause of the Great Famine (Kefu Qan) of 1888-92?

options.text: A rinderpest epidemic from Italian cattle imports through Massawa

questions.explanation: The immediate cause was a rinderpest epidemic triggered by Italian importation of infected cattle through Massawa.

questions.text: Who was the last king of Wolaita, arrested after resistance to Menilek's incorporation of the region in 1894?
questions.explanation: The Wolaita resistance was controlled after Kawo Tona, the last king of Wolaita, was arrested.

questions.text: Kafa was incorporated into the Ethiopian empire in 1897 after the defeat of which ruler?
questions.explanation: Kafa was incorporated in 1897 after the forces of Tato Gaki Sherocho, the last king of Kafa, were defeated.

questions.text: What was the first modern bank founded by Menilek II in 1905?
questions.explanation: Menilek II founded the first modern bank known as the Bank of Abyssinia in 1905.

questions.text: Which railway did Menilek II sign an agreement with the French to establish in 1894?
questions.explanation: Menilek signed an agreement and initiated work on the Addis Ababa-Djibouti railway with the French in 1894.

questions.text: Why did the British send a military expedition led by Sir Robert Napier to Ethiopia in 1868?

options.text: To free British/European citizens imprisoned by Tewodros
To support the Egyptians against Ethiopia
To build a railway to Massawa

questions.explanation: The British sent a large military expedition to free their citizens arrested by Tewodros.

questions.text: At which battle did about 8,000 of Tewodros's soldiers try but fail to check the advancing British forces in April 1868?
questions.explanation: On 10 April 1868, Tewodros's soldiers were defeated at the battle of Aroge.

questions.text: Who was the architect of Khedive Ismail's scheme to invade Ethiopia in the 1870s?
questions.explanation: Werner Munzinger was the architect of the whole of Ismail's scheme for the invasion of Ethiopia.

questions.text: At which battle did Emperor Yohannes IV's forces severely defeat the Egyptian army in November 1875?
questions.explanation: Yohannes IV and Ras Alula defeated the Egyptians at the Battle of Gundet on 16 November 1875.

questions.text: Italy's advance into northern Ethiopia (Mereb Melash) was decisively defeated in 1887 by Ras Alula Engida at which battle?
questions.explanation: They were defeated decisively at the Battle of Dogali by Ras Alula Engida in 1887.

questions.text: The Hewett Treaty of 1884 required Ethiopia to facilitate the evacuation of which trapped forces?

options.text: Egyptian soldiers encircled by the Mahdists in eastern Sudan

questions.explanation: Ethiopia agreed to facilitate the evacuation of Egyptian soldiers encircled by the Mahdists in eastern Sudan.

questions.text: Who signed the Wuchale treaty on behalf of Italy in 1889?
questions.explanation: The treaty was signed by King Menilek II and the Italian representative, Count Pietro Antonelli.

questions.text: What was the key discrepancy between the Amharic and Italian versions of Article XVII of the Wuchale treaty?

options.text: The Amharic version made use of Italian mediation obligatory, the Italian version optional
The Italian version made use of Italian mediation obligatory, the Amharic version optional

questions.explanation: The Amharic version said the emperor 'could' use Italian mediation while the Italian text made it obligatory.

questions.text: Who led the Ethiopian force that defeated the Italians at Amba Alage before the battle of Adwa?
questions.explanation: A force led by Fitawrari Gebeyehu Gurmu defeated the Italians at Amba-Alage.

questions.text: Approximately how many troops gathered at Wara-Illu after Menilek's proclamation for general mobilization before Adwa?
questions.explanation: About 100,000 troops from every part of the country gathered at Wara-Illu.

questions.text: Which country was the first to recognize Ethiopia's independence after the Battle of Adwa?
questions.explanation: By the treaty of Addis Ababa, Italy — the first country to do so — recognized the independence of Ethiopia.

questions.text: Who was crowned empress of Ethiopia after Lij Iyasu was deposed in 1916?
questions.explanation: Iyasu was deposed on September 27, 1916, and Zewditu, Menilek's daughter, was crowned empress.

questions.text: At which battle was Iyasu's father, Nigus Mikael, defeated and captured by the Shewan army led by Ras Teferi?
questions.explanation: Nigus Mikael was defeated and captured at Sagale on October 27, 1916, the deadliest battle since Adwa.

questions.text: The period of dual governance between Empress Zewditu and Ras Teferi Mekonnen after 1916 is known as:
questions.explanation: The political settlement of 1916 marked the start of the period of dual governance known as diarchy.

questions.text: Which document, adopted in 1931, provided the legal framework for Haile Selassie's emerging autocratic rule?
questions.explanation: The first written constitution of 1931 established the legal basis for Haile Selassie's emerging absolutism.

questions.text: Which region was permitted to retain rule by its own local hereditary chiefs under the 1931 Constitution?
questions.explanation: With the exception of Tigray, other provinces lost internal autonomy under the 1931 Constitution.

questions.text: At Walwal in the Ogaden, Ethiopian and Italian forces clashed on which date?
questions.explanation: Ethiopian and Italian forces clashed at Walwal on December 5, 1934.

questions.text: The two 19th century long-distance trade routes in Ethiopia both started from _______, the capital of the Kafa Kingdom.
questions.explanation: Both major trade routes started from Bonga, the capital of the Kafa Kingdom.

questions.text: The _______ Thaler was a coin introduced from Austria to the Horn of Africa region.
questions.explanation: The Maria Theresa Thaler (MTT) was a coin introduced from Austria to the Horn of Africa.

questions.text: Kassa Hailu of Quara took the throne name _______ upon his coronation in 1855.
questions.explanation: Kassa Hailu took the throne name Tewodros II, King of Kings of Ethiopia.

questions.text: Tewodros II established an arms manufacturing centre at _______, near Debre Tabor.
questions.explanation: Tewodros established an arms manufacture at Gafat, near Debre Tabor.

questions.text: Tewodros II's famous mortar produced at Gafat was nicknamed '_______'.
questions.explanation: His famous mortar produced at Gafat was known as 'Sebastopol.'

questions.text: Emperor Yohannes IV recognized Menilek as Nigus of Shewa in 1878 through the _______ Agreement.
questions.explanation: Yohannes IV recognized Menilek as Nigus of Shewa in 1878 by the Liche agreement.

questions.text: The Council of _______ in 1878 declared Tewahdo the only doctrine of the Ethiopian Orthodox Church.
questions.explanation: Yohannes IV presided over the Council of Boru Meda (1878).

questions.text: Emperor Yohannes IV died in 1889 fighting the Mahdists at _______.
questions.explanation: On 9 March 1889, Yohannes marched to Metemma where he died fighting the Mahdists.

questions.text: Ras _______ Dache played a pivotal role in Menilek's territorial expansion into Oromo territories.
questions.explanation: The Shewan Oromo notable Ras Gobana Dache played a pivotal role in territorial expansion.

questions.text: The western Gurage resistance to Menilek was led by Hassan Enjamo of _______.
questions.explanation: The western Gurage, led by Hassan Enjamo of Qabena, strongly resisted Menilek's forces.

questions.text: Ras Adal (Nigus Tekle-Haymanot) was defeated by Ras Gobana at the Battle of _______.
questions.explanation: Ras Adal was defeated at Embabo by Menilek's commander Ras Gobana.

questions.text: The Arsi Oromo resistance was finally suppressed at the battle of _______ on 6 September 1886.
questions.explanation: The Arsi resistance was suppressed at the battle of Azule on 6 September 1886.

questions.text: The combined Harari and Oromo forces resisting Menilek's expansion were defeated at the battle of _______ in 1887.
questions.explanation: Their forces were defeated at the battle of Chalanqo on 6 January 1887.

questions.text: The Great Famine of 1888-92 is also known in Amharic as _______.
questions.explanation: The Great Famine (1888-92) is also referred to as Kefu Qan.

questions.text: _______ was the last king of Wolaita, arrested after resistance in 1894.
questions.explanation: The Wolaita resistance was put under control after Kawo Tona, the last king of Wolaita, was arrested.

questions.text: Kafa was incorporated in 1897 after the defeat of _______, its last king.
questions.explanation: Kafa was incorporated after the forces of Tato Gaki Sherocho were defeated by Menilek's army.

questions.text: Menilek II founded the first modern bank in Ethiopia, called the Bank of _______, in 1905.
questions.explanation: Menilek II founded the Bank of Abyssinia in 1905.

questions.text: Menilek II signed an agreement with the French in 1894 to build the Addis Ababa-_______ railway.
questions.explanation: Menilek initiated work on the Addis Ababa-Djibouti railway with the French in 1894.

questions.text: The British military expedition of 1868 to free European captives from Tewodros was commanded by Sir Robert _______.
questions.explanation: The British sent a military expedition commanded by Sir Robert Napier in 1868.

questions.text: Tewodros committed suicide at _______ after the British stormed the fortress on April 30, 1868.
questions.explanation: Tewodros committed suicide at Maqdala after the British stormed the fortress.

questions.text: _______ was the architect of Khedive Ismail's scheme for the Egyptian invasion of Ethiopia.
questions.explanation: Werner Munzinger was the architect of the whole of Ismail's scheme for the invasion of Ethiopia.

questions.text: Ethiopian forces under Yohannes IV and Ras Alula defeated the Egyptians at the Battle of _______ in November 1875.
questions.explanation: The Egyptian troops were severely defeated at the Battle of Gundet on 16 November 1875.

questions.text: Italy's penetration of northern Ethiopia was decisively checked at the Battle of _______ in 1887.
questions.explanation: They were defeated decisively at the Battle of Dogali by Ras Alula Engida in 1887.

questions.text: The 1884 treaty brokered by the British between Ethiopia and Egypt is known as the _______ Treaty.
questions.explanation: The British brokered a treaty known as the Hewett Treaty between Ethiopia and Egypt in 1884.

questions.text: The Wuchale treaty was signed by Menilek II and the Italian representative Count Pietro _______.
questions.explanation: The treaty was signed by King Menilek II and Count Pietro Antonelli.

questions.text: The decisive Battle of Adwa was fought on March 1, _______.
questions.explanation: The last and decisive phase of the war was fought at Adwa on March 1st, 1896.

questions.text: By the Treaty of _______ signed on October 26, 1896, Italy recognized Ethiopia's independence.
questions.explanation: By the treaty of Addis Ababa signed on October 26, 1896, Italy recognized the independence of Ethiopia.

questions.text: Empress _______ is believed to have designed the strategy known as the siege of Mekelle.
questions.explanation: The siege of Mekelle strategy was believed to be designed by Empress Taytu.

questions.text: After Lij Iyasu was deposed in 1916, Menilek's daughter _______ was crowned empress.
questions.explanation: Zewditu, Menilek's daughter, was crowned empress of Ethiopia in 1916.

questions.text: Ras Teferi Mekonnen was crowned Emperor _______ in 1930, ending the period of diarchy.
questions.explanation: The coronation of Ras Teferi as Emperor in 1930, under the name Haile Selassie, marked the end of diarchy.

questions.text: Who devised the German war plan that proposed attacking France through Belgium before turning against Russia?
questions.explanation: The Germans followed a plan devised by Count Alfred von Schlieffen, their Chief of the General Staff.

questions.text: Where was the German advance halted in September 1914, starting a stalemate on the Western Front?

questions.text: What discovery, along with unrestricted submarine warfare, helped push the US to declare war on Germany in 1917?

questions.text: Which four imperial dynasties collapsed as a result of World War I?

options.text: Habsburgs, Hohenzollerns, Ottoman sultanate, and Romanovs

questions.explanation: Four imperial dynasties collapsed: the Habsburgs of Austria-Hungary, the Hohenzollerns of Germany, the Ottoman sultanate, and the Romanovs of Russia.

questions.text: The Treaty of Versailles between Germany and the Allied Powers was signed on which date?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Versailles was signed on June 28, 1919.

questions.text: Who were the members of the 'Big Four' at the Paris Peace Conference?

options.text: Wilson, Clemenceau, Lloyd George, and Orlando
Lloyd George, Trotsky, Wilson, and Orlando

questions.explanation: The Big Four were Woodrow Wilson (US), Georges Clemenceau (France), David Lloyd George (Britain), and Vittorio Orlando (Italy).

questions.text: As a result of the Treaty of Versailles, what happened to Germany's territories in Africa and the Pacific?

options.text: They were returned to Germany after 10 years
They became mandates administered by the League of Nations
They were annexed by the United States

questions.text: What was the most radical political group in Russia, following the teachings of Karl Marx?

questions.text: The Russian Social Democratic Labour Party later split into the Bolsheviks and which other faction?

questions.text: What was the immediate cause of the Russian Revolution of 1905?

options.text: Defeat by Japan in the Russo-Japanese War

questions.text: What document did Tsar Nicholas II issue after the Bloody Sunday massacre, purportedly creating a constitutional monarchy?
questions.explanation: Nicholas II was forced to issue the October Manifesto, turning Russia into a purported constitutional monarchy.

questions.text: Who led the Provisional Government formed after the February Revolution, before being succeeded by Alexander Kerensky?
questions.explanation: The Provisional Government was led by George Lvov, who was succeeded by Alexander Kerensky.

questions.text: What were the popular Bolshevik slogans that helped them win support in 1917?

options.text: 'All Power to the Soviets!' and 'Peace, Land and Bread!'

questions.text: The October 1917 Revolution led by the Bolsheviks began on which date?
questions.explanation: The Bolsheviks led a popular insurrection beginning on 25 October 1917.

questions.text: After seizing power, the Bolshevik regime was led by Premier Lenin and which war minister?
questions.explanation: The Bolsheviks established a regime led by Premier Lenin and war minister Leo Trotsky.

questions.text: What economic policy did the Bolsheviks introduce in 1921 to solve mounting economic problems?

questions.text: Who succeeded Lenin as leader of the Soviet Union after Lenin's death in 1924?
questions.explanation: Lenin died in 1924 and was succeeded by Joseph Stalin.

Britain, France, Russia, and the USA
Germany, Japan, Italy, and the USA

questions.explanation: Mussolini persuaded Yugoslavia to hand over the port of Fiume, acquiring it in 1924.

questions.explanation: He conquered Ethiopia in 1936, which sounded a death knell of the League of Nations.

Hostile French attitude over the Ruhr and reparations
Weimar Republic's acceptance of unfair treaties
Germany's early victory in World War I

questions.explanation: Japan attacked the US naval base at Pearl Harbor in December 1941, leading the USA to declare war on Japan.

questions.explanation: The victories at the Battles of Stalingrad (1942/3) and Kursk (1943) marked the beginning of the Allied counter-offensive.

questions.text: How many Shimageles (elders) are typically appointed by disputing parties in Shimgelina?
questions.explanation: In Shimgelina, five Shimageles (elders) would be appointed by the disputing parties themselves.

questions.text: Who often serves as chairman to make the Shimgelina process more acceptable to society?

options.text: A priest of the local church

questions.explanation: In most cases, a priest of the local church serves as chairman to make Shimgelina more acceptable.

questions.text: The Sidama Luwa system is administered by an age grade system where each grade rotates every how many years?
questions.explanation: The Luwa system is administered by an age grade system where each grade rotates every 8 years.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT one of the five rotating age grades in the Sidama Luwa system?
questions.explanation: The five Luwa age grades are Darara, Fullassa, Hirobora, Wawassa, and Mogissa — Gumaa is an Oromo term, not a Luwa grade.

questions.text: What is the primary objective of the Sidama Luwa system regarding able-bodied men?

options.text: Recruitment and training for national defence

questions.explanation: The first and most important objective of the Luwa system is recruiting and training able-bodied men for national defence.

questions.text: The Sidama moral code that provides the basis for distinguishing good from evil is called:
questions.explanation: The Sidama moral code halale provides the basis for distinguishing 'good' and 'evil'.

questions.text: In Kambata and Hadiya culture, what governs political administration, social involvement, and dispute resolution?
questions.explanation: In Kambata and Hadiya culture, Seera is the basis for political administration and dispute resolution.

questions.text: What are the three main types of heritage identified in the unit?
questions.explanation: There are different types of heritage: natural, tangible, and intangible heritages.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of intangible heritage?
questions.explanation: Fichee-Chambalaalla, a Sidama New Year celebration, is an intangible cultural heritage — the others are tangible sites.

questions.text: The Stelae of Aksum were included in the UNESCO List of World Heritage Sites in which year?
questions.explanation: Axum and its archaeological sites were included in the List of World Heritage Sites in 1980.

questions.text: The Rock-hewn Churches of Lalibela were registered by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site in which year?
questions.explanation: The Rock-hewn Churches of Lalibela were registered by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site in 1978.

questions.text: Fasil Ghebbi, the premise of King Fasiledes, is located in which town?
questions.explanation: Fasil Ghebbi is found in Gondar town, the Royal enclosure of King Fasiledes.

questions.text: The Simien Mountains National Park is home to which rare animals?

options.text: The Gelada baboon, Simien fox, and Walia ibex

questions.explanation: The Park is home to rare animals such as the Gelada baboon, the Simien fox, and the Walia ibex.

questions.text: The Lower Valley of Awash, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is significant for what kind of research?
questions.explanation: The Lower Valley of Awash is a site of Paleo-anthropological research.

questions.text: The Tiya archaeological site, listed as a World Heritage Site in 1980, contains how many monuments?
questions.explanation: The Tiya site contains 36 monuments, including 32 carved stelae covered with symbols.

questions.text: The historic walled city of Harar (Jugol) was built during the time of which ruler?
questions.explanation: The wall (Jugol) of Harar was built during the time of Emir Nur Ibn Mujahid in the 16th century.

questions.text: The Konso Cultural Landscape, inscribed on the World Heritage list in 2011, is characterized by:
questions.explanation: Konso Cultural Landscape is an arid property of stone-walled terraces and fortified settlements.

questions.text: Meskel (the Finding of the True Cross) was inscribed on the UNESCO intangible cultural heritage list in which year?
questions.explanation: Meskel was inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2013.

questions.text: Gadaa, the indigenous democratic socio-political system of the Oromo, was inscribed on UNESCO's intangible heritage list in which year?
questions.explanation: Gadaa was inscribed on the representative list of the intangible cultural heritage of humanity in 2016.

questions.text: Timket (Ethiopian Epiphany) became Ethiopia's how many-th entry on the UNESCO intangible cultural heritage list, inscribed in 2019?
questions.explanation: Timket became the fourth entry for Ethiopia in the list of UNESCO intangible cultural heritage in 2019.

questions.text: Which festival is described as being solely for girls and young women in Tigray and Amhara regions?
questions.explanation: Ashenda, Ashendiye, Shaday or Solel is the biggest cultural festival solely for girls and young women.

questions.text: Irreecha, the Oromo thanksgiving festival, is celebrated annually near which kind of location?

options.text: River banks or water and trees

questions.explanation: Irreecha is celebrated near the river bank or water and tree, at the beginning of Birra (spring).

questions.text: Ethiopian manuscripts have traditionally been written in which language?
questions.explanation: Ethiopia has a written tradition in the Ge'ez language, and manuscripts flourished after Christianity's introduction.

questions.text: What were the traditional writing materials for Ethiopian manuscripts?

options.text: Parchment from goatskin and ink from plants/minerals

questions.explanation: Writing materials included parchment from goatskin, ink from plants and minerals, and pens from reed or bamboo.

questions.text: The Temple of Yeha, dated to around 700 BC, was built in which architectural style?
questions.explanation: The Temple of Yeha is a tower built in the Sabaean style, dated to around 700 BC.

questions.text: The Sof Omar cave system was formed by which river changing its course?
questions.explanation: The Sof Omar cave system was formed by the Weyb River as it carved a new channel through limestone.

questions.text: The Halala Keela (Halala Kab) wall of Dawuro was bordered by which two rivers?

options.text: The Blue Nile and Tekeze Rivers

questions.explanation: The Dawuro wall was constructed on strategic defense positions, bordered by the Omo and Gojeb Rivers.

questions.text: What did Ethiopia have special schools for, in Gondar and Shewa, related to manuscript production?
questions.explanation: There were special schools for calligraphy in Gondar and Shewa, and a school for bookbinding.

questions.text: Indigenous knowledge is often known as '_______ knowledge'.
questions.explanation: Indigenous knowledge is often known as 'local knowledge'.

questions.text: The Afar people's indigenous conflict resolution mechanism is called _______.
questions.explanation: The indigenous mechanism of conflict resolution among the Afar is known as Mada'a.

questions.text: The Afar people's indigenous information exchange system is called _______.
questions.explanation: The Afar have an indigenous, unique information exchange system called Dagu.

questions.text: In the Gadaa system, the Oromo people are organized into five classes that succeed each other every _______ years.
questions.explanation: The five Gadaa classes succeed each other every eight years.

questions.text: The Oromo process of reconciliation carried out by a group of elders is called _______.
questions.explanation: Jaarsummaa is the process of reconciliation between conflicting individuals or groups by Jaarsaas.

questions.text: Among the Oromo, _______ refers to the blood money paid to a slain person's family.
questions.explanation: Gumaa refers to the blood money paid to the slain's family or compensation to injured individuals.

questions.text: The Oromo term for customary law and justice procedure is _______.
questions.explanation: Heera refers to customary law and justice procedure among the Oromo.

questions.text: _______ is a stick symbolizing a socially sanctioned set of rights exercised by Oromo women.
questions.explanation: Siinqee (Siiqee) is a stick symbolizing a socially sanctioned set of rights exercised by women.

questions.text: The main indigenous conflict resolution mechanism among the Amhara people is called _______.
questions.explanation: Among the Amhara people, the main indigenous conflict resolution mechanism is Shimgelina.

questions.text: In Shimgelina, _______ elders (Shimageles) are appointed by the disputing parties.
questions.explanation: In Shimgelina, five Shimageles (elders) would be appointed by the disputing parties.

questions.text: The Sidama age-grade institution, with grades rotating every 8 years, is called the _______ system.
questions.explanation: The Sidama Luwa system is an age-related institution with grades rotating every 8 years.

questions.text: The Sidama moral code providing the basis for distinguishing good and evil is called _______.
questions.explanation: The Sidama moral code halale provides the basis for distinguishing good and evil.

questions.text: In Kambata and Hadiya culture, the code of behaviour governing social life is called _______.
questions.explanation: Seera refers to the code of behaviour that is followed and internalized in Kambata and Hadiya culture.

questions.text: _______ Heritage refers to physical artifacts, buildings, and monuments passed from generation to generation.
questions.explanation: Tangible Heritage refers to physical artifacts, buildings and historic places transmitted from generation to generation.

questions.text: The Stelae of Aksum were included in the UNESCO List of World Heritage Sites in _______.
questions.explanation: Axum and its archaeological sites were included in the List of World Heritage Sites in 1980.

questions.text: The Rock-hewn Churches of _______ were registered by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site in 1978.
questions.explanation: The Rock-hewn Churches of Lalibela were registered by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site in 1978.

questions.text: Fasil Ghebbi, the premise of King Fasiledes, is found in the town of _______.
questions.explanation: Fasil Ghebbi is found in Gondar town.

questions.text: The Simien Mountains National Park is home to the Gelada baboon, the Simien fox, and the _______ ibex.
questions.explanation: The Park is home to the Gelada baboon, Simien fox, and Walia ibex.

questions.text: The Lower Valley of _______ is significant for Paleo-anthropological research, located in Afar Regional State.
questions.explanation: The Lower Valley of Awash is a site of Paleo-anthropological research located in Afar Regional State.

questions.text: The _______ archaeological site, listed in 1980, contains 36 monuments including 32 carved stelae.
questions.explanation: The Tiya site contains 36 monuments, including 32 carved stelae covered with symbols.

questions.text: The historic walled city of _______ (Jugol) was registered by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site in 2006.
questions.explanation: The Historic City of Harar (Jugol) was registered by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site in 2006.

questions.text: The Konso Cultural Landscape was inscribed on the World Heritage list in _______.
questions.explanation: The Konso Cultural Landscape was inscribed on the world heritage list in 2011.

questions.text: _______, the commemoration of the finding of the True Cross, was inscribed as intangible heritage in 2013.
questions.explanation: Meskel was inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2013.

questions.text: The _______ system, the Oromo indigenous democratic socio-political system, was inscribed by UNESCO in 2016.
questions.explanation: Gadaa was inscribed on the representative list of the intangible cultural heritage of humanity in 2016.

questions.text: Fichee-Chambalaalla, the Sidama New Year celebration, was inscribed as intangible heritage in _______.
questions.explanation: Fichee-Chambalaalla was inscribed on the representative list of intangible cultural heritage of humanity in 2015.

questions.text: _______, the festival marking the baptism of Jesus, became Ethiopia's fourth UNESCO intangible heritage entry in 2019.
questions.explanation: Timket (Ethiopian Epiphany) became Ethiopia's fourth entry on the UNESCO intangible cultural heritage list in 2019.

questions.text: Ethiopian manuscripts have traditionally been written in the _______ language.
questions.explanation: Ethiopia has a written tradition in the Ge'ez language.

questions.text: The Temple of _______, dated to around 700 BC, is built in the Sabaean architectural style.
questions.explanation: The Temple of Yeha is a tower built in the Sabaean style, dated to around 700 BC.

questions.text: The Sof Omar cave system was formed by the _______ River carving a channel through limestone.
questions.explanation: The Sof Omar cave system was formed by the Weyb River.

questions.text: There were special schools for _______ in Gondar and Shewa for manuscript production.
questions.explanation: There were special schools for calligraphy in Gondar and Shewa.

questions.text: A relation R from set A to set B is classified as a function if and only if:

options.text: Every element in set A is paired with exactly one element in set B
Every element in set B is paired with at least two elements in set A
The domain of R is strictly smaller than the codomain
The relation has no inverse mapping

questions.explanation: By definition, a function pairs each input from its domain with a unique output in its codomain.

questions.text: Which graphical test determines whether a curve in the Cartesian plane represents a function y = f(x)?
questions.explanation: If any vertical line intersects the graph at more than one point, a single x-value yields multiple y-values, so it is not a function.

questions.text: Given f(x) = 2x + 3 and g(x) = x² - 1, what is the composite value (f ∘ g)(2)?
questions.explanation: First compute g(2) = 2² - 1 = 3. Then f(g(2)) = f(3) = 2(3) + 3 = 9.

questions.text: For a function f to possess an inverse function f⁻¹, f must be:

options.text: A quadratic polynomial with positive leading coefficient

questions.explanation: An inverse function exists if and only if f is bijective (injective and surjective), ensuring a unique reverse mapping.

questions.text: According to the Remainder Theorem, dividing polynomial P(x) by (x - c) results in a remainder equal to:
questions.explanation: When P(x) = (x - c)Q(x) + R, evaluating at x = c yields P(c) = 0 · Q(c) + R = R.

questions.text: What is the degree of the polynomial function P(x) = 5x⁴ - 3x² + 7x - 9?
questions.explanation: The degree of a polynomial is the highest power of the variable x with a non-zero coefficient, which is 4.

questions.text: By the Factor Theorem, (x - 2) is a factor of P(x) = x³ - 4x² + x + 6 if:
questions.explanation: P(2) = 2³ - 4(2)² + 2 + 6 = 8 - 16 + 2 + 6 = 0, proving that (x - 2) is indeed a factor.

questions.text: How many complex roots (counting multiplicities) does a polynomial of degree n possess?
questions.explanation: The Fundamental Theorem of Algebra states that every non-zero single-variable polynomial of degree n has exactly n complex roots.

questions.text: What is the domain of the natural logarithmic function f(x) = ln(x)?
questions.explanation: Logarithms are only defined for strictly positive arguments, so the domain is all real numbers x > 0.

questions.text: If log₂(x) = 5, what is the value of x?
questions.explanation: Converting logarithmic form to exponential form: x = 2⁵ = 32.

questions.text: Which logarithmic property correctly rewrites log_b(M · N)?
questions.explanation: The product rule for logarithms establishes that log_b(M · N) = log_b(M) + log_b(N).

questions.text: What is the horizontal asymptote of the exponential curve f(x) = 3^x - 4?
questions.explanation: As x → -∞, 3^x approaches 0, so f(x) approaches 0 - 4 = -4, giving horizontal asymptote y = -4.

questions.text: What is the exact radian measure corresponding to 150°?
questions.explanation: Radians = degrees × (π / 180) = 150 × (π / 180) = 5π/6.

questions.text: Which fundamental Pythagorean identity holds true for all angle values θ?
questions.explanation: On the unit circle, x² + y² = 1 translates directly into cos²(θ) + sin²(θ) = 1.

questions.text: What is the period of the standard sine function y = sin(x)?
questions.explanation: The sine wave completes one full repeating oscillation every 2π radians.

questions.text: If angle θ lies in the second quadrant (Quadrant II), which trigonometric ratio is positive?
questions.explanation: In Quadrant II, y > 0 and x < 0; hence sin(θ) = y/r is positive while cos(θ) and tan(θ) are negative.

questions.text: What is the measure of an angle inscribed in a semicircle?
questions.explanation: By Thales's theorem, an inscribed angle intercepting a semicircle of 180° measures exactly half that arc: 90°.

questions.text: What is the relationship between a tangent line to a circle and the radius drawn to the point of tangency?

options.text: They are parallel to each other

questions.explanation: A tangent to a circle is always perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.

questions.text: What is the center and radius of the circle defined by (x - 3)² + (y + 5)² = 49?
questions.explanation: The standard form (x - h)² + (y - k)² = r² gives center (h, k) = (3, -5) and r = √49 = 7.

questions.text: What is the sum of opposite angles in any cyclic quadrilateral?
questions.explanation: The opposite angles of a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle always sum to 180°.

questions.text: What is Euler's polyhedron formula relating Vertices (V), Edges (E), and Faces (F)?
questions.explanation: Euler's characteristic for any convex 3D polyhedron states that V - E + F = 2.

questions.text: What is the formula for the volume of a right circular cone of radius r and height h?
questions.explanation: A cone has one-third the volume of a cylinder with the same circular base and perpendicular height: V = (1/3)πr²h.

questions.text: If a sphere has radius r = 3 cm, what is its total surface area?
questions.explanation: Surface area of a sphere is 4πr² = 4 · π · 3² = 36π cm².

questions.text: A pyramid has a square base with side length 6 m and height 10 m. What is its volume?
What is the Euclidean distance between points A(1, 2) and B(4, 6)?
What are the coordinates of the midpoint of segment joining P(-2, 8) and Q(6, 4)?
Two non-vertical lines are perpendicular if and only if the product of their slopes m₁ · m₂ equals:
questions.explanation: Perpendicular lines satisfy the negative reciprocal relationship m₁ · m₂ = -1.

questions.text: What is the perpendicular distance from point (x₀, y₀) to the line Ax + By + C = 0?
questions.explanation: The standard perpendicular point-to-line distance formula is d = |Ax₀ + By₀ + C| / √(A² + B²).

questions.text: Which of the following physical quantities is a vector?
questions.explanation: Vectors require both magnitude and direction; velocity specifies both.

questions.text: In a vector diagram, what does the length of the drawn arrow represent?
questions.explanation: The arrow length is proportional to the vector's magnitude.

questions.text: When adding two vectors graphically, what is the standard head-to-tail method?

options.text: Place the tail of the second at the head of the first

questions.explanation: The resultant is drawn from the tail of the first to the head of the second.

questions.text: Two perpendicular vectors have magnitudes 3 N east and 4 N north. The resultant magnitude is?
questions.explanation: Resultant magnitude is sqrt(3^2+4^2)=5 N.

questions.text: A vector of magnitude 6 N is directed at 60 degrees above the +x axis. Which of the following are its components?
questions.explanation: Fx = r cos theta, Fy = r sin theta; with r=6, theta=60°

questions.text: A vector is completely specified by its magnitude only.
questions.explanation: A vector requires both magnitude and direction for complete description.

questions.text: What is a unit vector and how is it used when resolving a vector into components?
questions.answerKey: A unit vector is a vector with magnitude 1 that points in a given direction. It is used to express a vector as a sum of its components along the coordinate axes, e.g., F = Fx î + Fy ĵ, where Fx = |F| cos(theta) and Fy = |F| sin(theta).
questions.explanation: Unit vectors provide direction along axes to separate a vector into components.

questions.text: List the basic steps of the graphical method of vector addition.
questions.answerKey: 1) Choose a scale and mark it. 2) Draw each vector tail-to-head in sequence. 3) Draw the resultant from the starting tail to the final head. 4) Measure the resultant’s magnitude and direction.
questions.explanation: Steps follow the tail-to-head construction; scale ensures accurate representation.

questions.text: A displacement vector has magnitude 12 m at 30 degrees north of east. Find its x and y components. Use +x east, +y north.
questions.explanation: Fx = r cos(theta) = 12 cos(30°) ≈ 10.39 m; Fy = r sin(theta) = 12 sin(30°) = 6.00 m.

questions.text: Two vectors A = 8 N at 45° and B = 5 N at 135°. Find the magnitude and direction of the resultant R.
questions.explanation: Resolve into components: Ax=8cos45≈5.66, Ay=8sin45≈5.66; Bx=5cos135≈-3.54, By=5sin135≈3.54; Rx≈2.12, Ry≈9.19; |R|≈√(Rx^2+Ry^2)≈9.43; θ=atan(Ry/Rx)≈77°.

questions.text: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Vectors have both magnitude and direction; displacement specifies a change in position with a direction.

questions.text: Which notation represents a vector quantity algebraically?

options.text: A bold letter such as A or an arrow over A

questions.explanation: Vectors are represented by a bold letter or an arrow over the letter to indicate direction.

questions.text: If vector A is 3 m east and vector B is 4 m north, their resultant has magnitude and direction approximately:
questions.explanation: Resultant magnitude is sqrt(3^2+4^2)=5 m; angle tanθ = 4/3 ⇒ θ ≈ 53.1° north of east.

questions.text: Which method is used to add two vectors graphically?
questions.explanation: Graphical addition is often performed using the parallelogram law (head-to-tail approach).

questions.text: A vector A has magnitude 10 N at 60° above the +x axis. Its x- and y-components are:
A scalar quantity has both magnitude and direction.
questions.explanation: Scalar quantities have magnitude only; vectors have both magnitude and direction.

questions.text: Give two examples of vector quantities and two examples of scalar quantities.
questions.answerKey: Vector: displacement, velocity; Scalar: mass, temperature
questions.explanation: Vectors require magnitude and direction; scalars require only magnitude and unit.

questions.text: Briefly outline the steps to add two vectors using the head-to-tail (parallelogram) method.
questions.answerKey: Draw both vectors from a common starting point; place the tail of one at the head of the other (head-to-tail); draw the resultant as the diagonal of the parallelogram; measure magnitude and direction using the chosen scale.
questions.explanation: Head-to-tail method is the graphical approach for vector addition.

questions.text: A force of 9 N is applied at 40° above the +x axis. Find the x- and y-components (to 2 decimals) and provide the final units.
Resolve a force of 12 N acting at 60° above the +x axis into x- and y-components.
Which of the following quantities is a vector?
questions.explanation: A vector quantity has both magnitude and direction. Mass, distance, and temperature are scalars with magnitude only.

questions.text: In a vector diagram drawn to scale, what does the length of the arrow represent?
questions.explanation: In vector diagrams, the length is proportional to the vector's magnitude; direction is shown by the arrowhead.

questions.text: Which operation corresponds to placing vectors head-to-tail to obtain the resultant?
questions.explanation: Adding vectors by the head-to-tail method yields the resultant vector.

questions.text: Resolving a vector into horizontal and vertical components uses which axes?
questions.explanation: Resolving a vector uses horizontal and vertical (x and y) components along the chosen axes.

questions.text: Two equal vectors of 6 N each act with an angle of 60 degrees between them. What is the magnitude of the resultant?
questions.explanation: R = sqrt(A^2 + A^2 + 2A^2 cosθ) with A=6, θ=60 gives R = 6√3 ≈ 10.39 N.

questions.text: Displacement and distance are the same when motion is in a straight line with constant direction.
questions.explanation: When motion is along a straight line with no direction change, net displacement equals distance travelled.

questions.text: Name two scalar quantities and two vector quantities.
questions.answerKey: Scalar: mass, temperature; Vector: velocity, force
questions.explanation: Scalar quantities have only magnitude; vector quantities have magnitude and direction.

questions.text: Resolve the 70 N force directed 150° from the +x axis into its x and y components.
Two vectors: A = 30 N directed east; B = 40 N at 60° north of east. Find the resultant magnitude and direction (from +x).
questions.answerKey: R ≈ 60.8 N at ≈ 34.7° north of east
questions.explanation: Decompose B into components: Bx=40 cos60=20; By=40 sin60≈34.64; R components: Rx=50, Ry=34.64; magnitude ≈ sqrt(50^2+34.64^2) ≈ 60.8 N; direction arctan(34.64/50) ≈ 34.7° north of east.

questions.text: Resolve a 40 N force acting at 30° above the +x axis into its horizontal (x) and vertical (y) components.
Which of the following quantities is a vector? (Distinct application example 31.)
questions.explanation: A vector has both magnitude and direction; temperature, mass, and time are scalars.

questions.text: Which statement correctly describes vector notation?

options.text: A bold letter denotes a vector quantity or an arrow over the letter indicates a vector; |S| denotes a scalar magnitude.
An arrow over a letter denotes a scalar value.
A bold letter always denotes a scalar quantity.
A vector has no magnitude, only direction.

questions.explanation: Vectors can be represented by bold letters or with an arrow; |S| gives only magnitude.

questions.text: A vector diagram is primarily used to show:

options.text: Only the magnitude of a vector
Only the direction of a vector
Both magnitude and direction with an arrow representing the vector
The position of the vector's tail at the origin

questions.explanation: Vectors are shown with arrows where length indicates magnitude and direction indicates orientation.

questions.text: Which method is used to add two vectors graphically? (Distinct application example 34.)
questions.explanation: Graphical addition places the tail of the second vector at the head of the first; the resulting vector is from tail to head of the two vectors.

questions.text: Which statement is true about resolving a vector into components?

options.text: A vector has only horizontal components
A vector can be resolved into horizontal and vertical components using trigonometric projections
Components are always equal in magnitude
Components do not depend on the angle of the vector

questions.explanation: Components depend on the angle; use cos for horizontal, sin for vertical (assuming angle from x-axis).

questions.text: Scalars require both magnitude and direction for a complete description.
questions.explanation: Scalar quantities have magnitude only; direction is not required for a complete description.

questions.text: Explain how to resolve a force of 5 N at 30° north of east into horizontal and vertical components.
questions.answerKey: Fx = 5 cos 30° ≈ 4.33 N (east); Fy = 5 sin 30° ≈ 2.50 N (north). The components are found using F cosθ for horizontal and F sinθ for vertical, with angles measured from the +x axis (east).
questions.explanation: Use standard component resolution: Fx = F cosθ, Fy = F sinθ.

questions.text: A boat travels 6.0 km at 20° north of east, then 8.0 km at 60° north of east. Find the magnitude and direction of the resultant displacement.
questions.answerKey: Resultant displacement: components: x = 6 cos20 + 8 cos60 = 5.638 + 4.000 = 9.638 km; y = 6 sin20 + 8 sin60 = 2.052 + 6.928 = 8.980 km. Magnitude ≈ 13.2 km; direction ≈ arctan(8.980/9.638) ≈ 43.6° north of east.
questions.explanation: Use vector components and Pythagoras to obtain resultant magnitude and arctan for direction.

questions.text: Two displacement vectors A and B have magnitudes 5.0 m and 7.0 m and are at an angle of 40° to each other. What is the magnitude of their resultant displacement? Provide all values, units, and context.
Resolve a displacement vector of magnitude 12.0 m directed 25° north of west into its x (horizontal) and y (vertical) components. Provide the components with correct signs and units.
questions.explanation: Vx = 12 cos25° toward west (negative x); Vy = 12 sin25° toward north (positive y).

questions.text: A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 2 m/s^2 for 5 s. What is the displacement during this interval?
Displacement is best described as:

options.text: a) the total distance travelled along the path
b) final position minus initial position
c) the average speed over the interval
d) the magnitude of the velocity vector

questions.explanation: Displacement is a vector describing the straight-line change in position from the initial to the final point, not the path length.

questions.text: A particle’s position is given by s = 2t^2 + 3 (m). What is the average velocity from t = 0 to t = 5 s?
On a velocity-time graph that rises linearly from 0 to 20 m/s over 4 s, what is the acceleration?
questions.explanation: Acceleration is the slope of the v–t graph: a = Δv/Δt = (20 − 0)/4 = 5 m/s^2.

questions.text: A car starts from a speed of 4 m/s and accelerates at 3 m/s^2 for 6 s. It then continues at a constant speed for 4 s. What is the total displacement in 10 s?
The instantaneous velocity is the slope of the position-time graph.
questions.explanation: The instantaneous velocity at a specific time is given by the slope of the position-time graph at that time.

questions.text: Define acceleration.
questions.answerKey: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity with respect to time.
questions.explanation: Acceleration describes how velocity changes per unit time (a = Δv/Δt).

questions.text: What does the slope of a velocity-time graph represent?
questions.explanation: The slope of the velocity-time graph corresponds to the acceleration (for constant acceleration).

questions.text: A car starts from rest and accelerates at 3 m/s^2 for 5 s, then decelerates at -2 m/s^2 for 4 s. What is the final velocity after the 9 s, and the total displacement during those 9 s? Provide the numerical values with units.
questions.answerKey: Final velocity: 7 m/s; Total displacement: 81.5 m

questions.text: A particle starts with velocity 12 m/s and accelerates uniformly at 0.5 m/s^2 for 10 s. What is the displacement during the 10 s? Provide the numerical answer with units and brief method.
A car increases its velocity from 0 to 20 m/s in 4 s. What is its average acceleration?
questions.explanation: Average acceleration a_avg = Δv/Δt = (20 − 0)/4 = 5 m/s^2.

questions.text: A ball starts from rest and accelerates at 2 m/s^2 for 3 s. How far does it travel in that time?
In a velocity-time graph for an object with constant acceleration, what does the slope represent?
questions.explanation: For constant acceleration, a is the slope of v vs t.

questions.text: A car starts at 5 m/s and accelerates at 1 m/s^2 for 6 s. Its final velocity is
An object with initial speed u = 4 m/s accelerates at a = 2 m/s^2. It covers a displacement of s = 80 m in a straight line. What is the time t required? Use s = ut + 0.5 a t^2.
If velocity changes uniformly with time, acceleration is constant.
questions.explanation: Uniform rate of velocity change implies constant acceleration.

questions.text: Explain the difference between average velocity and instantaneous velocity.
questions.answerKey: Average velocity is displacement divided by the time interval; instantaneous velocity is the velocity at a specific instant (the limit as the time interval approaches zero).
questions.explanation: Average velocity uses a finite time interval; instantaneous velocity is the velocity at a single moment.

questions.text: Describe how the displacement relates to the area under a velocity-time graph for motion with changing velocity.
questions.answerKey: Displacement equals the area under the velocity-time graph; positive area corresponds to forward motion, negative area to backward motion.
questions.explanation: Area under v-t graph represents net displacement during the time interval.

questions.text: A car starts from rest (u = 0) and accelerates at a = 1.5 m/s^2 for t = 8 s. What distance does it cover? Provide all values, units, method, final unit.
An object with initial velocity u = 4 m/s accelerates at a = 2 m/s^2. It covers a displacement s = 80 m in a straight line. Find the time t required.
A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 3 m/s^2 for 4 s. What is its final velocity?
questions.explanation: Using v = u + at with u = 0, a = 3 m/s^2, t = 4 s; v = 0 + 3×4 = 12 m/s.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about constant acceleration is true?

options.text: The velocity changes at a constant rate
The velocity is zero at all times

questions.explanation: Constant acceleration means the rate of change of velocity is constant; velocity changes at a constant rate.

questions.text: The velocity–time graph of an object with constant acceleration is a straight line.
questions.explanation: With constant acceleration, velocity changes linearly with time, producing a straight-line v-t graph.

questions.text: Which equation gives the displacement s after time t for an object with initial velocity u and constant acceleration a?
questions.explanation: For constant acceleration, displacement s = ut + (1/2) a t^2 is the standard equation.

questions.text: An object starts from speed u = -5 m/s and accelerates at a = 3 m/s^2 for t = 4 s. What is the displacement s during this interval?
Define average velocity and instantaneous velocity, and explain how they differ.
questions.answerKey: Average velocity is total displacement divided by total time; instantaneous velocity is the velocity at a specific time, equal to the slope of the position-time graph at that time.
questions.explanation: Average velocity uses overall displacement/time; instantaneous velocity uses the slope at a specific moment on a position-time graph.

questions.text: A particle starts from u = 10 m/s and accelerates uniformly at a = -2 m/s^2 for t = 6 s. Find the displacement s in this interval. Provide your answer with units.

A car moves east with initial speed u = 15 m/s and experiences a constant westward acceleration a = -3 m/s^2 for t = 6 s. What is the displacement s during this interval? Provide your answer with units.
Explain how instantaneous velocity is determined from a position-time graph and how it relates to average velocity.
questions.answerKey: Instantaneous velocity is the slope of the position-time graph at a single time; average velocity is the total displacement divided by the total time.
questions.explanation: The slope at a single time gives instantaneous velocity; average velocity uses whole interval.

questions.text: The displacement–time graph for an object undergoing uniform acceleration is which of the following, and what does the slope represent?

options.text: A straight line; slope represents velocity
A straight line; slope represents acceleration

questions.explanation: The displacement-time (s-t) graph for uniform acceleration is a parabola; the slope at any time is the instantaneous velocity.

questions.text: In one dimension, displacement is:

options.text: A) the distance travelled along the path
B) the final position minus the initial position without direction
C) the straight-line difference between final and initial positions with direction
D) the rate of change of velocity

questions.explanation: Displacement is the vector from the initial to the final position, including direction; it equals the change in position x2−x1 along the straight line joining the points.

questions.text: A car speeds up from v = 0 to v = 20 m/s in 4 seconds with constant acceleration. What is the acceleration?
questions.explanation: Acceleration a = Δv/Δt = (20 − 0) / 4 = 5 m/s^2.

questions.text: Which equation would you use to relate displacement s, initial velocity u, acceleration a, and time t to find velocity after time t?

options.text: B) s = u t + 1/2 a t^2

questions.explanation: In constant acceleration, velocity after time t is v = u + a t.

questions.text: On a velocity-time graph for uniformly accelerated motion, the area under the curve between t1 and t2 represents:
questions.explanation: The area under a velocity-time graph over a time interval equals the displacement during that interval.

questions.text: Two trains move in the same direction with speeds 20 m/s and 15 m/s. The relative speed of the second with respect to the first is:
questions.explanation: Relative speed is the difference of speeds when moving in the same direction: 20 − 15 = 5 m/s.

questions.text: The equation s = u t + 1/2 a t^2 is valid for any motion.
questions.explanation: That equation is valid only for motion with constant acceleration.

questions.text: Explain what instantaneous velocity means and how it differs from average velocity.
questions.answerKey: Instantaneous velocity is the velocity at a specific instant in time (the slope of the position-time curve at that instant). It can differ from the average velocity, which is the total displacement over a time interval divided by the length of that interval. In uniformly accelerated motion, instantaneous velocity changes with time, while average velocity over an interval equals the average of the initial and final velocities over that interval.
questions.explanation: Instantaneous velocity = v(t0); average velocity over [t1,t2] = (v1 + v2)/2 for constant acceleration.

questions.text: Describe how the slope and the area on a velocity-time graph relate to acceleration and displacement in uniformly accelerated motion.
questions.answerKey: The slope of the velocity-time graph gives acceleration; the area under the velocity-time graph over a time interval gives displacement.
questions.explanation: For v(t) = u + at, slope = a; area under v(t) from t1 to t2 = ∫ v dt = displacement.

questions.text: A cart starts with velocity 5 m/s and accelerates at 2 m/s^2 for 4 s. Find its final velocity and displacement.
questions.explanation: Final velocity: v = u + a t = 5 + 2×4 = 13 m/s. Displacement: s = ut + 1/2 a t^2 = 5×4 + 1/2×2×16 = 20 + 16 = 36 m.

questions.text: A car accelerates at 2 m/s^2 for 5 s, then coasts (a = 0) for 3 s. Find the total displacement in the first 8 s.
questions.explanation: First 5 s: s1 = ut + 1/2 a t^2 = 0 + 1/2×2×25 = 25 m; velocity after 5 s: v1 = 0 + 2×5 = 10 m/s. Next 3 s: s2 = v1 × 3 = 10 × 3 = 30 m. Total s = 25 + 30 = 55 m.

quizzes.title: Physics — Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body Quiz
quizzes.subject: Physics

questions.text: A simply supported beam AB of length 3.0 m carries a downward load W = 90 N acting at its midpoint and an additional downward point load P = 20 N located 0.5 m from the left end A. The beam is supported at A and B. Which of the following gives the correct reaction forces at the supports A and B?
questions.explanation: Sum of vertical forces: RA+RB = 110 N. Moments about A: RB*3.0 = 90*1.5 + 20*0.5 = 145 → RB ≈ 48.3 N. Then RA ≈ 61.7 N.

questions.text: In static equilibrium, the sum of moments about any point on the body is zero.
questions.explanation: For equilibrium, both the resultant force and the resultant moment must be zero; thus the moments about any chosen point sum to zero.

questions.text: Which statement best distinguishes elastic deformation from plastic deformation?

options.text: Elastic deformation is permanent; plastic deformation is recoverable.
Elastic deformation is recoverable after removing the load; plastic deformation is permanent.
Both are always reversible regardless of load history.
Only plastic deformation occurs under tensile loading.

questions.explanation: In elasticity, materials return to original shape after unloading; plastic deformation leaves permanent shape change.

questions.text: Which statement correctly defines the Young's modulus of a material in the elastic region?

options.text: It is the ratio of strain to stress.
It is the ratio of stress to strain in the elastic limit.
It is the product of stress and strain.
It is the sum of stress and strain.

questions.explanation: Young's modulus E = σ/ε in the elastic region; measures stiffness.

questions.text: State the SI unit of density and briefly explain what it represents.
questions.explanation: Density is mass per unit volume; the SI unit is kilograms per cubic meter (kg/m^3).

questions.text: Describe the difference between stress and strain.
questions.answerKey: Stress is force per unit area; strain is the fractional change in dimension (deformation) of a body.
questions.explanation: Stress (σ) is the internal force per area; strain (ε) is the relative deformation ΔL/L or similar measures.

questions.text: A simply supported beam AB of length 5.0 m is supported at A and B. A downward load W = 150 N acts at the midspan (2.5 m from A). A further downward load P = 60 N acts at x = 1.0 m from A. Calculate the reactions at A and B.
questions.explanation: Sum of forces: RA+RB = 210 N. Moments about A: RB*5.0 = 150*2.5 + 60*1.0 = 435 → RB ≈ 87 N. RA ≈ 210 - 87 = 123 N.

questions.text: A wire of length L = 2.0 m and cross-sectional area A = 1.0×10−4 m^2 is stretched by a force F = 1000 N, producing an extension ΔL = 0.0005 m. Calculate the Young’s modulus E. Provide the method and final unit.
Which statement about the stress-strain curve for a material in the elastic region is true?

options.text: A. The slope (stiffness) decreases as strain increases.
B. The stress is independent of strain.
C. Stress is proportional to strain, with a constant slope equal to Young's modulus.
D. The area under the curve is zero.

questions.explanation: In the elastic region, Hooke's law holds: σ = Eε; slope equals E.

questions.text: Specific gravity of a substance is defined as the ratio of its density to the density of water at 4°C. What is its unit?
questions.explanation: Specific gravity is a ratio of densities, so the units cancel; SG is dimensionless.

questions.text: In static equilibrium of a rigid body, which statement is true?

options.text: The resultant of all external forces on the body is zero.
The sum of all external moments on the body is zero.
The velocity of the body is zero at all times.
The potential energy of the body is minimized in every configuration.

questions.explanation: This reflects the First Condition of Equilibrium: the net force on the body must be zero for equilibrium, which also implies no linear acceleration.

questions.text: Young's modulus is defined as E = stress divided by strain. Which of the following is the correct statement?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus relates stress and strain in the elastic region: E = σ/ε. The unit is Pascal (Pa).

questions.text: Elastic limit is defined as the maximum stress that can be applied to a material without causing:

options.text: Elastic rebound to a larger shape

questions.explanation: Beyond the elastic limit, permanent (plastic) deformation occurs; within the elastic limit, the material returns to its original shape when the load is removed.

questions.text: A block has density 7800 kg/m^3 while water has density 1000 kg/m^3. What is its specific gravity (relative to water)?
questions.explanation: Specific gravity is the ratio of the object's density to the density of water (rho_block / rho_water).

questions.text: A uniform rod of length 2 m with weight 20 N is hinged at its left end. It is held horizontally by a rope attached to the right end making an angle of 30° above the horizontal. If in equilibrium, what is the tension T in the rope?
questions.explanation: Taking moments about the hinge: T sin(30°) × 2 m = 20 N × 1 m. With sin(30°)=0.5, T × 1 = 20 → T = 20 N.

questions.text: The second condition of equilibrium requires that the sum of moments about any point must be zero.
questions.explanation: The second condition states that the net moment (torque) about any point is zero for equilibrium.

questions.text: Explain briefly what is meant by the first condition of equilibrium and give a simple example from a static, rigid-body situation.
questions.answerKey: First condition: the vector sum of all external forces on a body equals zero so there is no linear acceleration. Example: a door held closed by a frictionless hinge and a magnetic latch where the hinge force balances the latch force, keeping the door at rest.
questions.explanation: First condition: the vector sum of all external forces on a body equals zero so there is no linear acceleration. Example: a door held closed by a frictionless hinge and a magnetic latch where the hinge force balances the latch force, keeping the door at rest.

questions.text: Define strain and describe the difference between tensile and compressive strain.
questions.answerKey: Strain is the fractional change in length (ΔL/L0) due to applied stress. Tensile strain stretches the material (ΔL>0); compressive strain shortens it (ΔL<0).
questions.explanation: Strain is the fractional change in length (ΔL/L0) due to applied stress. Tensile strain stretches the material (ΔL>0); compressive strain shortens it (ΔL<0).

questions.text: A solid of volume 0.002 m^3 is completely submerged in water. Given water density 1000 kg/m^3 and g = 9.81 m/s^2, calculate the buoyant force on the block. Provide the method and final unit.
questions.answerKey: Buoyant force F_b = ρ_water × g × V_sub = 1000 × 9.81 × 0.002 = 19.62 N
questions.explanation: Buoyant force equals the weight of the displaced water (Archimedes' principle). Here V_sub = 0.002 m^3, ρ_water = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2; F_b = 19.62 N.

questions.text: A solid block of volume 0.004 m^3 has density 900 kg/m^3. What is its weight? Provide the method and final unit.
questions.explanation: Mass m = density × volume; m = 900 × 0.004 = 3.6 kg. Weight W = m g = 3.6 × 9.81 ≈ 35.3 N.

questions.text: In static equilibrium, the vector sum of all forces acting on a rigid body must be what?

options.text: Forces must pass through the same point.

questions.explanation: First condition of equilibrium states that the net force is zero (∑F = 0) for a body to be in equilibrium.

questions.text: Which option correctly defines Young's modulus?

options.text: The ratio of longitudinal stress to longitudinal strain in the elastic region.
The ratio of longitudinal strain to longitudinal stress in the elastic region.
Force divided by the cross-sectional area.
Mass divided by the volume of the material.

questions.explanation: Young's modulus E is defined as stress over strain in the elastic (linear) region.

questions.text: Which statement about static equilibrium is true?

options.text: The resultant force must be zero but moments may be nonzero.
The resultant moment must be zero but forces may be nonzero.
Both the resultant force and the resultant moment must be zero.
Both the resultant force and resultant moment can be nonzero.

questions.explanation: A body in static equilibrium has zero net force and zero net moment about any point.

questions.text: If a rod is stretched within its elastic limit and the applied force is doubled while the cross-sectional area remains constant, what happens to the Young's modulus (E)?

options.text: Doubling the force doubles both stress and strain, leaving E unchanged.
Doubling the force doubles stress but leaves strain unchanged.
Stress remains unchanged and strain doubles.
Doubling both stress and strain would double E.

questions.explanation: Within the elastic region, E remains constant for a material; doubling the force increases both stress and strain proportionally, so E stays the same.

questions.text: For static equilibrium, the sum of moments (torques) about any point must be zero.
questions.explanation: Second condition of equilibrium requires zero net torque about any point.

questions.text: Specific gravity of a liquid is

options.text: The ratio of the density of the liquid to the density of water at a reference temperature
The mass of water displaced by the liquid
The ratio of pressure to volume of the liquid

questions.explanation: Specific gravity is density divided by density of water at a reference temperature; it is unitless.

questions.text: Define elastic deformation and plastic deformation.
questions.answerKey: Elastic deformation is a reversible deformation that disappears when the load is removed; plastic deformation is permanent, remaining after removing the load (beyond the elastic limit).
questions.explanation: Elastic deformation is recoverable; plastic deformation results in permanent shape change after unloading.

questions.text: State the second condition of equilibrium and describe how you would verify it for a rigid body using torque about a chosen point.
questions.answerKey: The second condition states that the sum of moments (torques) about any axis/point must be zero for equilibrium. To verify, compute the torques of all forces about a chosen point and ensure their algebraic sum is zero; if not, adjust unknowns (e.g., support reactions) until the sum is zero.
questions.explanation: For a body in equilibrium, both the net force and the net moment are zero; torque balance about any point ensures rotational equilibrium.

questions.text: A steel rod of length L = 2.0 m and cross-sectional area A = 1.0e-4 m^2 is stretched by a force F = 500 N along its length. The measured extension ΔL = 0.0005 m. Calculate Young's modulus E.
A uniform beam of length 3.0 m and weight 120 N is simply supported at its ends A and B. The weight acts at the midpoint of the beam. Determine the vertical reaction forces at A and at B.
questions.explanation: Take moments about A: RB × 3.0 m = 120 N × 1.5 m → RB = 60 N. Then RA = W − RB = 60 N.

questions.text: Which statement describes the first condition of equilibrium for a rigid body in static equilibrium?

options.text: A) The net external force on the body is zero.
B) The net external torque about any point is zero.
C) The body must be at rest.

questions.explanation: In static equilibrium, the resultant force must be zero; this is the first condition of equilibrium.

questions.text: Young's modulus is defined as
questions.explanation: Young's modulus E = stress/strain; it measures material stiffness.

questions.text: A sample with density 900 kg/m^3 has a specific gravity of 0.9. Which of the following represents specific gravity?
questions.explanation: Specific gravity is the ratio of density to density of water (1000 kg/m^3).

questions.text: In static equilibrium, which statement is true about torques (moments)?

options.text: A) The net force must be zero.
B) The sum of torques about any point must be zero.
C) Both net force and torque must be zero.
D) The body can rotate if the net torque is nonzero.

questions.explanation: The second condition of equilibrium states that the sum of torques about any point must be zero (in addition to net force being zero).

questions.text: Which statement best describes elastic deformation?

options.text: A) It is permanent and cannot be recovered.
B) It is reversible; the material returns to its original shape when the load is removed.
C) It only occurs in plastics and ceramics.
D) It increases with time under constant load.

questions.explanation: Elastic deformation is reversible; plastic deformation is permanent.

questions.text: In static equilibrium, the resultant force must be zero and the resultant torque must also be zero.
questions.explanation: Yes. Both net force and net torque must be zero for static equilibrium of a rigid body.

questions.text: Describe in one sentence the difference between the first and second conditions of equilibrium.
questions.answerKey: First condition: net external force is zero; Second condition: sum of moments (torques) about any point is zero.
questions.explanation: The first condition ensures no net force; the second ensures no net rotational effect.

questions.text: Describe, in two to three sentences, how Young's modulus can be determined experimentally using a wire and measurement of extension under known loads.
questions.answerKey: Use E = (F/A) / (ΔL/L) = (F L) / (A ΔL); apply a known weight F to a wire with cross-sectional area A and length L, measure extension ΔL, then compute E. The resulting unit is Pa (N/m^2).
questions.explanation: This method uses Hooke's law for a rod; E relates stress and strain.

questions.text: A uniform horizontal rod of length 2.0 m weighs 60 N is supported by two vertical ropes at its ends. The left rope has a tension of 30 N. Find the tension in the right rope.
questions.explanation: Sum of vertical forces: T_left + T_right = W; thus T_right = 60 - 30 = 30 N. Taking moments about the left end: T_right * 2.0 m = W * 1.0 m; T_right = 30 N. Both methods yield 30 N.

questions.text: A horizontal beam 6.0 m long is supported at its ends A and B. A 200 N weight acts at 2.0 m from A. Determine the reactions at supports RA and RB.
questions.explanation: Take moments about A: RB * 6.0 = 200 * 2.0 => RB = 66.7 N. Then RA = 200 - 66.7 = 133.3 N.

quizzes.title: Physics — Static and Current Electricity Quiz
quizzes.subject: Physics

questions.text: Charge exists in nature as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Charges come in two types: positive and negative; like charges repel, unlike attract.

questions.text: Which method charges a body by rubbing with another material?
questions.explanation: Charging by friction occurs when two insulators rub together, transferring charge.

questions.text: An electroscope is used to detect what?
questions.explanation: An electroscope detects the presence and magnitude of static charges by leaf divergence.

questions.text: Electrical discharge through air occurs due to what process?
questions.explanation: Discharge through air happens when air becomes ionized, allowing charge flow.

questions.text: Ohm's Law relates V, I, and R by V = I R. If R is constant and voltage doubles, what happens to current?
questions.explanation: I = V/R; with R fixed, doubling V doubles I.

questions.text: Inside a conductor in electrostatic equilibrium, the electric field is zero.
questions.explanation: In electrostatic equilibrium, charges rearrange to cancel internal electric fields.

questions.text: Where should a voltmeter be connected to measure potential difference across a component?
questions.explanation: A voltmeter measures across the component, so it is connected in parallel.

questions.text: What is the role of a switch in an electric circuit?
questions.answerKey: To open or close the circuit, controlling current flow.
questions.explanation: A switch toggles connectivity, turning devices on or off by completing or breaking the circuit.

questions.text: Two point charges q1 = +3 μC and q2 = -5 μC are separated by r = 0.20 m. Calculate the magnitude of the electrostatic force between them. Use k = 8.99×10^9 N m^2/C^2. Show steps and final unit.
A 12 V source is connected to a network where R1 = 6 Ω is in series with the parallel combo of R2 = 3 Ω and R3 = 6 Ω. Find the total current drawn from the source.
questions.explanation: Parallel of 3 Ω and 6 Ω is (3×6)/(3+6) = 2 Ω. Total R = 6 Ω + 2 Ω = 8 Ω. I = V/R = 12/8 = 1.5 A.

questions.text: According to Ohm's law, which statement is true?

options.text: A) The current is directly proportional to the voltage for a given resistance.
B) The current is inversely proportional to the voltage for a given resistance.
C) The voltage is independent of resistance.
D) The resistance is independent of temperature.

questions.explanation: Ohm's law is V = IR. For a fixed resistance, current I is proportional to voltage V. The other statements misstate the relationships.

questions.text: The direction of the electric field around a positive point charge is:

options.text: C) perpendicular to the radial direction

questions.explanation: Electric field lines emanate outward from a positive charge, showing the field direction away from the charge.

questions.text: In a simple circuit with a battery and a resistor, where should the ammeter be placed to measure current?

options.text: A) In parallel with the resistor
B) In series with the resistor

questions.explanation: An ammeter must be in series with the component whose current you want to measure so that the same current flows through both.

questions.text: Two resistors of 6 Ω and 3 Ω are connected in parallel to a 12 V source. What is their equivalent resistance?
questions.explanation: For parallel resistors, 1/R_eq = 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/6 + 2/6 = 3/6 = 1/2, so R_eq = 2 Ω.

questions.text: If you double the distance between two charges, the electrostatic force between them becomes:
questions.explanation: Coulomb's law F ∝ 1/r^2; doubling r makes F decrease by a factor of 4.

questions.text: An ideal voltmeter should be connected in series with the component whose voltage it is measuring.
questions.explanation: A voltmeter should be connected in parallel with the component to measure its voltage without significantly altering the circuit.

questions.text: State Ohm's law and define the symbols V, I and R.
questions.answerKey: Ohm's law states V = IR, where V is the voltage across the element, I is the current through it, and R is the resistance.
questions.explanation: Ohm's law relates voltage, current, and resistance; V is voltage, I is current, R is resistance.

questions.text: Explain how increasing resistance affects current in a circuit with fixed voltage.
questions.answerKey: Increasing resistance reduces current because I = V/R; for constant V, I decreases as R increases.
questions.explanation: With a fixed voltage, increasing R lowers the current according to Ohm's law.

questions.text: A 9 V battery is connected across a 3 Ω resistor. What is the current in the circuit? Show your calculation.
questions.explanation: Using Ohm's law I = V/R, I = 9 V / 3 Ω = 3 A. Final unit: amperes (A).

questions.text: Two resistors, 3 Ω and 6 Ω, are in series with a 12 V supply. What is the current in the circuit? Show your calculation.
questions.explanation: Total resistance R = 3 Ω + 6 Ω = 9 Ω. Current I = V / R = 12 V / 9 Ω = 1.33 A (approx).

questions.text: Which method of charging a body involves rubbing two insulating materials together to transfer charge?
